brief: Goldman's IG credit trading desk argues the week's price action overstates the damage. The street was net lifted on 1.3bn of risk Friday and ETFs traded an orderly 0-1bp to NAV, yet IG100 still closed 10bps wider, tied for its worst week of the year. IG cash underperformed its implied beta (+10bps vs +6bps expected) while CDXIG outperformed (+6bps vs implied +8.6bps), which the author reads as credit investors broadly onsides and the cash move exaggerated by thin seasonal liquidity. Separately, hyperscaler credit's correlation to IG100 has risen to 0.93 from a 0.74 average, at 2x beta versus a 1.5x average, which the author attributes to broad macro de-risking rather than hyperscaler-specific selling, unlike the mid-summer AI-capex-funding-driven underperformance. Goldman and Apollo priced a $44bn multi-tranche SpaceX GPU financing deal that held up despite Friday's selloff, even as IG selling concentrated in the 3-7y curve and high-yield spreads widened 51bps; the author expects next year's chip-financing supply to crowd out generic high-yield demand. A separate update reports record de-grossing, a 9.8/10 vol panic reading, and 5-year-low leverage. Near-term, the author leans tactically bullish on IG credit after the move wider but prefers selling volatility over owning cash for upside.
